title: The Orpheus Group
summary: A company that sends agents among the dead.

claims.text: Project Echo is the Group's work on finding, making and using projectors.
Its agents have their own slang; its researchers coin more technical words, and agent slang is far more common.
A horror show is an illegal job in which a client pays Orpheus to frighten a target into madness or a possibly fatal accident.
A beach is a break between missions, usually a week or more; a snow job is a mission that looks too easy.
A fumigation is a mission to clear a place of spooks, usually by destroying them.

title: Projectors
summary: Living people whose spirits can leave the body.

claims.text: A projector is a living human whose spirit can leave the body and travel.
Skimmers project by yogic technique; going zero is leaving the body, and ripcording is snapping back at once, which harms the body and is kept for desperate escapes.
Sleepers are agents who have been flatlined and kept in cryogenic suspension; their tubes are cradles, or coffins.
The body a projector leaves behind is called the meat. Death merchants are freelance mercenary projectors.

title: Ghosts: Spirits and Hues
summary: The two kinds of ghost among the player Laments.

claims.text: Ghosts are spooks who do not project. Spirits are the common kind; hues used pigment in life and differ from spirits.
Spook covers ghosts and projectors alike, anyone in gauze or without a body.
Drones are ghosts with Vitality 1, called repeaters; blips have 2 or 3 and are near-functional, called reactives.
Jasons are living people taken over by mad spooks or Spectres who then kill like serial killers.

title: Laments
summary: A character's kind of ghost or projector.

claims.text: A Lament is a character's race: ghost or projector, each with two subsets.
Laments decide much less of a character than Nature and role do; each character is meant to stay an individual.

title: Shades
summary: The five templates that shape a ghost's outlook.

claims.text: There are five Shades: Banshee, Haunter, Poltergeist, Skinrider and Will-o-the-Wisp.
Agent slang: a Banshee is a screamer, a Haunter a squatter, a Poltergeist a breaker, a Skinrider a control freak or puppetmaster, a Wisp a flicker.
Someone a Skinrider rides or controls is called a Malkovich.

title: Vitality
summary: A spook's life force and body at once.

claims.text: Vitality and Spite are the two central traits of every character.
A spook's body is the projection of its soul's emotional state, so Vitality is both its energy and its body.
Sharing Vitality within a crucible is called networking.

title: Spite and Stains
summary: The darkness that builds in a spook.

claims.text: Spite is the negative energy and feeling that gathers in a spook's soul.
When Spite rises above Vitality, the character starts slipping away from the person they think they are.
Stains are changes to the ghostly form when insecurity and fear warp the sense of self; each makes the character less human.
Stains come to those who often give way to rage or bitterness, but they often give some protection or advantage.

title: Horrors
summary: The powers of ghosts and projectors.

claims.text: Horrors are the powers projectors and ghosts use.
Thorns are a Spectre's innate powers.
Special effects, or F/X, is agent code for any Horror or Stain in public.
Manifesting is appearing to and acting on the living.

title: Pigment
summary: A new street drug tied to the dead.

claims.text: Pigment, also called black heroin, is a cheap, addictive hallucinogen popular with casual users such as students and ravers.
Pigment addicts are deadheads, and agents dislike them because they seem able to see spooks.

title: Crucible
summary: A team of spooks working together.

claims.text: A crucible is a circle of ghosts and projectors whose different aims are made to work together.
Crucibles usually have high Vitality. A rave is a fight among several spooks; the Big Bad is a powerful spook leading others or controlling living people.

title: The Shroud and the Wastelands
summary: What lies beyond death, as the living understand it.

claims.text: The Shroud is the veil between this world and the one thought to lie past it; some call it the Stormwall.
The Wastelands are a rumoured land of the dead being torn apart by the Maelstrom on the far side of the Shroud.
The Maelstrom was a great event some years ago that swept many ghosts away; little is known of it but rumour.
The Nothing is a ghost rumour of what follows a ghost's utter destruction; there is no evidence either way.
Gauze, or plasm, is a spook's body; the Quick are the living.

title: The Orpheus Series
summary: A limited game told in a set run of books.

claims.text: The game is a limited run that builds like a suspense film, each supplement a new revelation toward a final climax.
The run goes Crusade of Ashes, Shades of Gray, Shadow Games, The Orphan-Grinders, and End Game.
